Jordan —

Thanks for the quick read. Attached is a staged offer (redwood_staged_offer_v2.pdf) and a tighter MAP workbook that ties pricing bands to three checkpoints (MAP-v1.xlsx). Key summary below:

Checkpoint 1 — Pilot kickoff (2 weeks): no commit, nominal usage credits to cover testing (up to 250k tokens).
Checkpoint 2 — Pilot acceptance (functional & perf): customer commits to a 6-month NPU (committed-processing units) baseline; triggers 15% discount on list for committed units; unlocks access to dedicated capacity.
Checkpoint 3 — Production ramp (month 3+): committed ramp to 3x baseline in month 6 triggers an additional 10% tiered discount and optional enterprise support add-on.

Changes from the draft you saw: we replaced a single discount with a two-tier ladder so discounts flow from checkpoint approvals rather than upfront. We also included a limited credit (one-time) if the pilot extends beyond the initial window.

Action items for you:
- Confirm acceptance criteria for Checkpoint 2 (we suggested SLOs + evaluation prompts).
- Introduce procurement/legal contacts so we can push the final offer with redlines.

I’m available tomorrow 9–11 PT to review.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0199

Rishi — quick internal note before we push v3:

I reviewed the pricing ladder. Two small recommendations to make procurement happier and reduce friction at signature:

1) Add an explicit "fail-safe" clause: if pilot acceptance extends >60 days, a capped extension credit applies (e.g., 10% credit up to $10k).
2) Offer a mid-tier commit option (3-month bridge) between the 6-month baseline and the full ramp; this helps buyers with budgets that renew quarterly.

Also flagging legal: we should get Acme's standard redlines early — ask Jordan to share. We can pre-seed our counterparty responses.

If you want, I can draft the revised pricing table and swap the language on "dedicated capacity" to "optional dedicated pool" to avoid SLA commitments until legal signs off.

-M

Rishi — appreciate the updates. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Checkpoint 2 acceptance must include: 99th perc latency under 600ms for our 512-token prompts, and no more than 1.5% regression on the eval prompt set we supplied.
- Procurement wants the discount ladder in an easy-to-compare table (committed monthly units vs discount %) and a single line showing the initial committed monthly spend.
- Legal will circulate their redlines (I’ve looped Tara and procurement). Expect the redlines doc early next week.

Also, to push this faster: if Redwood can offer a 20% one-time credit applied upon successful checkpoint 2 acceptance (to offset initial integration cost), that would materially help our execs approve the 6-month commit. Is that something you can accommodate?

Jordan

Jordan / Tara / Procurement team —

Attached: redwood_staged_offer_v3.pdf and MAP-v2-staging-checkpoints.xlsx (updated). Summary of commercial changes in this revision:

- Checkpoint triggers preserved (Pilot kickoff; Pilot acceptance; Production ramp).
- We added a 20% one-time integration credit applied to the first invoice upon successful Checkpoint 2 acceptance (as requested).
- Discount ladder: 0–500k tokens/month = list; 500k–2M tokens/month = 15% off list after commit; >2M tokens/month = 25% off list after ramp trigger. We included a 3-month bridge commit option at 70% of the 6-month baseline price as Marissa suggested.
- Capped extension credit: 10% credit up to $10k if pilot extends beyond 60 days.
- Acceptance criteria: we adopted your latency/regression SLOs and embedded them in the MAP workbook (see tab "Acceptance").

Next steps / asks:
1) Procurement: can you confirm the committed monthly spend line (we put a placeholder $30,000/month for the 6-month baseline) or send your number and we'll lock it into the SOW?
2) Acme Legal: please send redlines to redlines_acme_legal.docx; we will pre-seed counterpoints in the attached file so signature can be fast.
3) Jordan: confirmation that Checkpoint 2 acceptance criteria look good to you as written so we can move to DocuSign onboarding.

We are happy to move to a canary production runway once Checkpoint 2 is accepted; the commercial concession (20% credit) is conditional on that acceptance and the mutually agreed eval prompts in the MAP workbook.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to run the pricing table if helpful.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
